'''Isabelle Gallagher''' (born 27 October 1973) is a French mathematician. Her research concerns [[partial differential equation]]s such as the [[Navier–Stokes equations]], the [[wave equation]], and the [[Schrödinger equation]], as well as [[harmonic analysis]] of the [[Heisenberg group]].<ref name="rencontre">{{citation|url=http://images.math.cnrs.fr/Rencontre-avec-Isabelle-Gallagher.html|title=Rencontre avec Isabelle Gallagher|language=French|trans-title=Meeting with Isabelle Galagher|first=Emmanuel|last=Ferrand|publisher=CNRS|work=Images des mathématiques: La recherche mathématique en mots et en images|date=5 April 2009|access-date=2 April 2016|archive-date=23 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190723005431/http://images.math.cnrs.fr/Rencontre-avec-Isabelle-Gallagher.html|url-status=dead}}.</ref><ref name="pdeb"/>

==Education and career==
Gallagher was born on 27 October 1973, in [[Cagnes-sur-Mer]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.math.jussieu.fr/~gallagher/cv.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae: Isabelle Gallagher|accessdate=3 October 2015}}.</ref> She earned her PhD from [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] in 1998. Her dissertation, supervised by [[Jean-Yves Chemin]], concerned [[fluid dynamics]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=55937}}</ref>

She worked at the French [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] and then, in 2004, became a professor at [[Paris Diderot University]].<ref name="rencontre"/>

She was elected president of the [[Société mathématique de France]] in June 2024. 

==Recognition==
In 2008, the [[French Academy of Sciences]] awarded her the [[Prix Paul Doistau–Émile Blutet]].<ref name="pdeb">{{citation|url=http://www.sciencesmaths-paris.fr/en/isabelle-gallagher-rewarded-by-the-academy-of-sciences-311.htm|title=Isabelle Gallagher rewarded by the Academy of Sciences|publisher=Fondation Sciences Mathématiques de Paris|accessdate=3 October 2015|archive-date=3 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160603075803/http://www.sciencesmaths-paris.fr/en/isabelle-gallagher-rewarded-by-the-academy-of-sciences-311.htm|url-status=dead}}.</ref> 

She was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2014.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|publisher=[[International Mathematical Union]]|accessdate=3 October 2015|archive-date=24 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124141541/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|url-status=dead}}.</ref> 

She won the [[CNRS Silver Medal]] in 2016.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.cnrs.fr/insmi/spip.php?article1614|title=Médailles d'argent, de bronze et de cristal|date=26 February 2016|publisher=CNRS, Inst. nat. des sciences mathématiques et de leurs interactions|accessdate=27 February 2016}}.</ref>

She was awarded the [[Sophie Germain Prize]] in 2018<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 November 2018 |title=Plaquette des Grands Prix de l'Académie des sciences 2018 |trans-title=2018 Academy of sciences Grand Prizes Brochure |url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/pdf/documentation/prix2018/plaquette_2018.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221215143957/https://www.academie-sciences.fr/pdf/documentation/prix2018/plaquette_2018.pdf |archive-date=15 December 2022 |access-date=24 March 2026 |website=[[French Academy of Sciences]] |language=fr |format=PDF}}</ref> by the [[French Academy of Sciences]].
